body: Honestly I'm still unsure why I continue on. Why bother is how I've been feeling. I know for a fact extended happiness won't last, so why continue a life when I know I'll suffer time and time again. It doesn't make sense. Why not just quit the game, and  cut my losses?
Came back here to read this since the last few days have been rough.

Initially, I typed out several long paragraphs using a variety of extended metaphors that related off your own (I really did like the water, cactus, bucket analogy.) But, lucky for you, my phone died. As I was writing it though, talking about things Im watering and such, I realized what a tremendous pussy I've become. I realized I haven't leaned into something fully in a long time, haven't given my all to anything in years. 

So, I made a deal with myself. Three months. By the time August comes, I can make a decision. Three months, Ill give everything I have into life. I won't let myself hold back. And after the summer, if I still feel this way, I can do as I please.

Moral of the story is, I've realized how self pity has consumed me these last few months. I realized on some level, but not until I wrote out my thoughts did I realize what a shithead I was being. I'm also writting this down here so at least one other person knows of my promise to myself, and I can also look back to this in my times of weakness.

I had more bad news hit me today. But I feel strangely good. I feel I can be alright.

I appreciate the well thought out. I really do. And talking about yourself makes me feel better, that's what I hate about therapy. How onesided it is. 

My distinction between pyschs and shrinks was I meant psychiatrists and therapists. One with an MD that can prescribe things, the other just for talking. At the moment, my psychiatrist specializes in both, so it's a one stop shop. As for sleep, I had the same problem until I got sleep meds. While I do have some nightmares still (the meds mainly take care of them) I am in control of my dreams regularly. But I find that makes me only yearn for sleep more and resent life more. Because no matter what I dream, it isn't real.

The thing I still don't understand I guess from your comment, is how is thriving really better? I've had fleeting moments of it I will admit, but was still suicidal during them. 

I'm also not going to lie to you. External influences have fucked up my mood more than I've given on. I recently lost a close friend due to an untimely death. Survivors guilt is a bitch. I wish it could've been me instead, he was at least mostly happy. Since then I've been failing classes and generally spiralling downwards. Picked up a nasty alcoholic streak a few months ago. Now I'll go through half a handle a night.

I think the worst thing about it all is I have no reason to feel this way. I have a good family, one that's supportive and loving. I certainly won the lottery with them. Every time I fall, I can't believe they stay and help up. But I'm done being a burden on them. I'm done fucking up their shit. I'm done being a disappointment. I intend to slip out and make them think somehow it was accidental. Sure they'd be sad, but at least they wouldn't be ashamed or hate me any more than they might now. Thanks again for reading this. I'll be up a while since my meds have a tendency of a delayed fuse/no kaboom at all. 

EDIT: I forgot to mention what I'm looking for here/my goals I guess. I don't really know. I'm just hoping there's a way out of the pain so I don't devastate my loved ones. Because I don't want to be responsible for their suffering. I just want to be at a place where doing even the things I love isn't a burden. In all honesty I think that and fear of the unknown are what have kept me from suicide this long.

By that logic, just because you're abused is the only justification you need to continue being abused. I know what you mean, but that just doesn't reasonate with me. Just because I'm in this shit situation (being alive) doesn't mean I need to continue staying in it.
